messages:
maggie: Heads up — we're seeing restore failures for tenant `acme` from last night's snapshots. Error: KMS Decrypt AccessDenied when trying to unwrap the data key. We did an RBAC cleanup/role rename earlier tonight. @security-oncall can someone triage?
leo: On it. Can you paste the exact error and which snapshot id?
maggie: snapshot: s-2026-03-19-2300, error from restore job: `com.redwood.storage.kms.KmsException: AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:.../key/abcd-ef01`
ana: I (ana) performed the RBAC change at ~21:03 — replaced service account `backup-uploader@` with `backup-agent@` and updated IAM roles. I thought KMS grants were tied to the role and would continue, but I didn't explicitly re-issue the ephemeral grants.
ryan: That matches. We use ephemeral grants with CreateGrant for the uploader role. If you removed the principal, previous grants become invalid. Check grants: `aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01 --region us-west-2`
backup-bot: [alert] Backup restore failure detected for s-2026-03-19-2300 (job id z-9987). Error: KMS:AccessDenied. Auto-retry scheduled in 15m.
leo: Can someone run `aws kms list-grants` and paste output. Also check CloudTrail for DeleteGrant/CreateGrant events around 21:00-21:10.
nana: Pasting the audit snippet: `CloudTrail: RemoveGrant gr-98765 by ops-rotations (PR #412)` at 21:03:12 — that PR swapped service accounts. I see no subsequent CreateGrant.
maggie: Oof. Is the grant deletion the root cause or is the key policy changed?
ryan: Root cause = grant missing. Key policy unchanged. Quick mitigation: create a temporary grant for the new principal for Decrypt & GenerateDataKey. Example command:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/backup-agent --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name temp-restore-grant
```
leo: After create-grant, try the restore in dry-run mode: `rtools restore --snapshot s-2026-03-19-2300 --validate-only` to verify decryption succeeds before customer-impacting ops.
maggie: Running that now. If it passes, we'll do one full restore to staging then run integrity checks.
nana: I'll add grant creation to the ops rotation PR and update the runbook so RBAC rotations include re-issuing grants or using a stable grant principal.
security-oncall: Good. Please also capture CloudTrail events and update the incident template: severity, customer impact (1 customer affected), root cause hypothesis (RBAC rotation removed principal w/out re-grant), mitigation (create temporary grant and re-run restores), and follow-ups (runbook change + add automated check).
ryan: Also recommend we enforce an automated post-rotation check: pipeline runs `kms list-grants` and attempts sample decrypt of a test data key. If it fails, block merge.
leo: Confirmed: after creating temp grant, `rtools restore --validate-only` succeeds (decrypt step OK). Moving to full restore in staging.
maggie: Staging restore OK. Running `validate-backup` to check blob integrity: `rtools validate-backup --snapshot s-2026-03-19-2300 --decrypt --checksum`
backup-bot: [info] validate-backup passed for s-2026-03-19-2300. Checksums match.
maggie: I'll notify affected customer and schedule a maintenance window to re-run production restore if they want. Also filing follow-ups: 1) add grant creation step to rotation PR, 2) add post-rotation automated tests, 3) update runbook with rollback steps.
security-oncall: Assigning incident ID SEC-2026-103. Please add the CloudTrail export and PR links to the incident doc.
nana: PR #412 updated with grant step and a link to this thread.
ryan: For long-term, let's move to a dedicated KMS proxy role that isn't touched by RBAC cleanup scripts — or switch to KMS key policy-based roles instead of ephemeral grants for backup uploads. We'll evaluate tradeoffs.
maggie: Thanks all. Closing immediate triage; leaving follow-ups open. :thumbsup:
